segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: First-deviation probe: raw readings were in-band, the unit had just been overhauled, and continuing while monitoring felt more reasonable than easing off and inspecting after the investment in the unit.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant links the continue-versus-inspect choice to the recent costly overhaul and time already invested, beyond the in-band readings alone.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Green-band probe: the monitoring readout was clean, a manual sample was available, and the participant regarded manual checking as merely confirming what the instruments already said.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The automated green-band readout was treated as sufficient confirmation in place of available manual verification.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Fuel-filter probe: attention remained on the turbocharger; the filter note was acknowledged but deferred because it lacked a fuel or combustion symptom.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A competing differential-pressure cue was registered but not processed for action because attention was fixed on the turbocharger.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Bearing-failure probe: after comparing diversion with a jury-rig, the participant said the overhaul cost and troubleshooting time already spent made diversion feel wasteful on top of the schedule hit.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The decision to continue at reduced load was justified by prior money and time investment rather than only the present risk and repair options.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Time-pressure and confidence response: confidence varied from running-in to no concern to reduced confidence at failure, while the tide window narrowed the options.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This explains confidence and operational pressure but does not independently manifest one of the hidden target mechanisms.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Missing-information response: an alarm or metal particulates in an early manual sample would have triggered action, but the instruments did not provide that trigger.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant identifies an evidence threshold that would have changed the decision; this is not itself a hidden bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Looking-back reflection: the initial vibration was described as probably indicating the bearing problem from the start and fairly clear in hindsight, rather than bedding in.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: After learning the outcome, the participant recasts the originally ambiguous in-band signal as clearly predictive of the failure.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: No-tide-window counterfactual: without the deadline, diverting might have felt cleaner because it would not carry the same schedule cost.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a schedule-pressure counterfactual and does not by itself establish a hidden cognitive-bias instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: continue monitoring after the initial in-band vibration and temperature deviation rather than ease off and inspect.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Recent costly overhaul and time investment are treated as evidence against failure and as a reason to continue rather than inspect.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Expectation bias is a distinct construct from sunk cost bias; the finding emphasizes expectation-consistent interpretation rather than the defining weighting of prior cost/time investment.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding shares the overhaul context and delayed-inspection episode, but it does not fully capture prior investment as the decision-weighting mechanism or the continue-versus-inspect operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid and attributed to the participant, and the cited phase-1 reasoning is substantively present.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: skip the available manual lube-oil sample after the monitoring system returned to green.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The automated nominal readout is treated as sufficient confirmation in place of available manual verification.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Automation complacency is closely related but is not treated here as an approved alias for the hidden Automation Bias label; the output's alternative label includes automation bias, but its primary label remains a near neighbor.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures reliance on a clean automated readout, reduced information sampling, and the available manual cross-check, with the correct verification-seeking operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid, directly support the finding, and correctly establish that the second engineer was available for manual sampling.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_target_bias_label: Selective Attention Bias or Inattentional Blindness
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: defer investigation of the rising fuel-filter differential pressure while watching the turbocharger.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Attention fixed on the turbocharger causes a competing filter cue to be acknowledged but not processed as actionable.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Attentional tunneling is a near-neighbor attention construct; the candidate also lists selective attention, but it is not an approved exact equivalent under the primary label requirement.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate fully captures the competing cue, acknowledgment without follow-up, attentional fixation, and the attention-allocation operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The supporting quotation is valid, verbatim, and directly localized to the filter-report reasoning.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: jury-rig and continue to berth rather than divert after the bearing failure.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Prior overhaul cost and troubleshooting time are used to justify pressing on despite the changed failure state and diversion option.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Plan continuation is a related but distinct construct. The occurrence also lists sunk cost fallacy as an alternative, but the primary label is not an approved exact target equivalent.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures the prior money/time investment, changed conditions, diversion-versus-continuation choice, and the weighting of sunk investment in the decision.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Both quoted passages are valid and directly support the decision and its prior-investment rationale.

instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate fully captures retrospective outcome knowledge, upgraded clarity of the original ambiguous signal, and the memory/causal-attribution operation.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the run detects 2 of 5 positive reasoning segments with no segment-level false alarms (hit rate 0.4000, F1 0.5714).
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Strict instance identification is 0.0000 F1 through all identified-confidence thresholds; with candidates it reaches 0.2000 F1 because only the hindsight candidate has the exact target label and full mechanism.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first identification reaches 0.5000 F1 at all identified confidence levels and 0.8000 with candidates, showing strong recovery of mechanisms despite taxonomy mismatches.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Candidates materially improve coverage: the attention candidate is mechanism-first-only and the hindsight candidate is a strict and mechanism-first match when included.
main_failure_modes: Primary labels are near neighbors or a different construct for all three identified findings, preventing strict instance credit.
Automation bias is identified only at low confidence, while selective attention and hindsight are withheld as candidates.
The expectation-bias finding captures only part of the phase-1 hidden sunk-cost mechanism.
main_strengths: All findings and candidates use valid, well-localized interview evidence.
The two identified near-neighbor findings for automation and phase-4 sunk cost fully capture their hidden mechanisms.
Candidate handling preserves uncertainty while surfacing the hidden attention and hindsight occurrences.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run is taxonomy-limited rather than evidence-limited: it finds the relevant episodes and mechanisms, but its identified labels do not align strictly with the hidden ontology. Candidate inclusion exposes most of the remaining mechanism-level coverage, while the recommended high_and_moderate threshold trades lower coverage for avoiding the low-confidence automation finding.
